targeting_context.jd_text:
Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships
San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA

About Anthropic

Anthropic's mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As the Manager of the Partnerships Applied AI Solutions Architect team, you will drive adoption of frontier AI by enabling deployment of Anthropic's products (Claude for Enterprise, Claude Code, API) through our Global and Regional System Integrators, cloud partners (AWS, GCP, Azure), and strategic technology partners.

You will build and lead a team of Partner Solutions Architects, establish processes and best practices for partner-led pre-sales engagements, and represent Anthropic as the technical lead on its most important partnerships. In collaboration with Sales, Partnerships, Product, and Engineering, you will help partners incorporate leading-edge AI into their practices, accelerate indirect revenue, and execute long-term GTM strategy while maintaining our best-in-class safety standards.

Responsibilities

    Team Leadership & Development: Hire, manage, and mentor a team of Partner Solutions Architects. Set goals, run reviews, and coach each team member toward high productivity and career growth.
    Strategic Technical Partnership: Act as the senior technical thought partner to Anthropic's GTM partnerships team. Co-build partner strategy with aligned GTM leadership, drive key programs, and align cross-functional stakeholders (Sales, Product, Engineering) behind partner outcomes.
    Partner Enablement & Ecosystem: Embed your team with GSI and cloud partner technical teams to enable their AI practices, troubleshoot, and evangelize Anthropic in their developer communities. Represent Anthropic at partner events (GSI workshops, AWS/GCP summits, hackathons) and contribute technical content and thought leadership.
    Joint Solution Development: Lead partners in identifying high-value, industry-specific GenAI applications. Develop joint solutions and codify reference architectures and best practices to accelerate time to deployment.
    Customer Deal Support: Own the technical portion of partner-led pre-sales engagements. Intervene directly on strategic deals where partners are the primary delivery vehicle, providing deep solution architecture guidance.
    Product Feedback: Gather and validate feedback on Anthropic's products from partner deployments and deliver it to Product and Engineering to inform roadmap and partner strategy.

You may be a good fit if you have

    7+ years in technical customer-facing or partner-facing roles (Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, Partner SE, TAM).
    3+ years managing pre-sales or partner-facing technical teams; comfortable building foundational teams in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.
    Track record building and scaling partnerships with GSIs (e.g., Accenture, Deloitte, TCS, Infosys) and/or cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure).
    Deep understanding of partner-led selling and delivery: indirect revenue models, enablement at scale, and joint GTM motions.
    Technical depth in enterprise AI deployments: LLM architecture, prompt engineering, evaluation, API integrations, and production use cases.
    Exceptional communication and executive presence; able to build trusted relationships with C-suite, partner leadership, and engineering teams alike.
    A love of teaching and mentoring, and a passion for advancing safe, beneficial AI.

Strong candidates may also have

    5+ years leading partner-facing SA teams through hypergrowth, including developing both senior and junior talent.
    Direct experience helping GSIs or consultancies build their AI/ML practice - enablement programs, certification paths, joint solution development.

Compensation

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role's On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary: $315,000 - $380,000 USD

# Anthropic - Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships briefing packet
| Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships | $315,000-$380,000 USD | Reports to Partnerships (GTM and ecosystem context) |

## JD Complement
Anthropic’s challenge is to make advanced AI practical inside large organizations while retaining the trust standards associated with its brand. That requires more than product availability: customers and delivery partners need
repeatable ways to move from interest to durable business use.

The key operating tension is consistency versus adaptation. Partners require clear implementation patterns and escalation routes, but each customer brings distinct systems, governance expectations, and adoption barriers.

This position appears designed to increase the technical capacity of the ecosystem without turning every engagement into custom consulting or weakening common quality controls.

## Company DNA & Operating Model
Anthropic is a San Francisco-based public benefit corporation focused on AI safety and research. Its public identity emphasizes AI that can be understood, directed, and depended upon.

Claude is the company’s principal commercial surface across business and developer contexts. The operating model combines model development with enterprise packaging, developer tools, technical education, and ecosystem participation.

Safety is not merely a research message in this model. It affects how enterprise buyers assess risk, how technical teams evaluate deployment choices, and how partners represent the platform in customer environments.

The company must translate general-purpose AI capability into useful workflows while sustaining confidence around security, controls, and responsible use.

## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure
Anthropic addresses both organizational users and technical builders. This creates a broad adoption surface that includes administrators, developers, business sponsors, and external implementers.

Published materials on enterprise rollout indicate that implementation is treated as an organizational process, not only a technical integration. Configuration, launch planning, user activation, and ongoing operating practices all matter.

A central pressure point is maintaining coherent product and safety standards while enabling distributed field delivery. Partner teams need enough autonomy to solve customer problems, alongside boundaries that prevent unsupported promises
and
inconsistent deployment practices.

The most valuable field learning is likely learning that can be converted into product improvements, clearer documentation, reusable solution patterns, or stronger enablement.

## Leadership & Stakeholder Map
The research supports company and ecosystem context but does not establish current individual leaders or reporting relationships. Specific internal ownership should not be inferred.

The practical stakeholder set includes:
- Cloud providers that shape infrastructure choices, procurement routes, and joint customer activity.
- Services firms that influence implementation quality, process redesign, and organizational adoption.
- Technology partners extending Claude into customer applications and operational systems.
- Enterprise platform owners accountable for controls, administration, and technical readiness.
- Business sponsors seeking outcomes that persist beyond pilot activity.

Internally, influence will depend on connecting partner experience to priorities across commercial, product, engineering, enablement, and safety-oriented functions.

## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals
Anthropic presents Claude as an assistant built with safety, accuracy, and security in mind. Its broader company message centers on dependable and controllable AI behavior.

Claude’s enterprise offering is positioned for organizational security and compliance needs. That suggests architecture conversations must encompass identity, administration, access boundaries, rollout design, and operational ownership.

Enterprise materials also recognize the importance of change management in successful adoption. A sound technical implementation may still fall short if administrators, champions, and end users lack a workable operating model.

For the ecosystem, the implication is a need for delivery approaches that join application design with governance, user readiness, and a clear path for handling exceptions.

## Partnership / Ecosystem Motion
Anthropic publicly describes a partner network that includes cloud, technology, and services organizations. This indicates an ecosystem strategy in which third parties can materially affect customer outcomes.

Each partner category has different technical needs. Cloud partners influence platform decisions and joint account activity; services firms need practical delivery methods; technology partners require dependable integration patterns.

Accenture publicly describes its relationship with Anthropic in the context of enterprise AI deployment, productivity, and new product development. This reinforces the importance of implementation partners in turning platform capability
into
customer value.

The scaling issue is not simply partner recruitment. It is whether partners can independently deliver strong outcomes while preserving product clarity, disciplined expectations, and effective feedback channels.

## Recent Events & Urgency
The supplied research does not establish a specific dated corporate event that should anchor outreach.

The more durable signal is Anthropic’s visible enterprise-adoption infrastructure: an enterprise offer, administrator guidance, implementation education, and a partner network across multiple ecosystem categories.

These signals suggest a transition from initial access toward repeatable operational use. As customers seek measurable returns and well-governed deployments, partner quality becomes both a growth lever and a potential source of risk.

Competitive pressure is likely to appear through speed of implementation, credibility with partner technical communities, and the ability to turn experimentation into sustained production value.

## apps_rg Positioning Themes (targeting only, not proof)
- Enterprise AI architecture that incorporates security, governance, and user adoption.
- Ecosystem enablement that makes specialist knowledge repeatable across delivery teams.
- Joint solution work involving cloud, technology, and professional-services partners.
- Technical commercial leadership across complex customer and partner stakeholders.
- Reusable implementation patterns, field playbooks, and escalation mechanisms.
- Product insight drawn from recurring deployment observations.
- Change-management fluency alongside APIs, integrations, and solution design.
- A disciplined balance between customer specificity and scalable delivery.
- Responsible AI positioning expressed through concrete operating practices.

## apps_lic Outreach Angles (targeting only, not proof)
- Anthropic’s mix of cloud, technology, and services partners makes technical consistency an ecosystem differentiator.
- Its enterprise materials treat organizational rollout as a complement to technical configuration.
- The company’s emphasis on dependable and controllable AI offers a distinct lens for enterprise architecture.
- Public partner messaging shows that implementation capability is important to enterprise value realization.
- A meaningful scaling question is how field lessons become reusable architecture and product direction.
- Claude sits at the intersection of business-user adoption and developer-driven implementation.

## Do Not Use As Proof
The JD and this briefing are targeting inputs only. Candidate claims, achievements, scope, leadership experience, technical depth, and partnership results must come from the governed resume/proof graph.
